question.problem:
Calls to a customer service center occur continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of one call every $10$ minutes. If no calls have been received for $20$ minutes, what is the probability that the next call will come within the next $5$ minutes? Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**

The required probability is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Since calls occur continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next call using the exponential distribution.

Let $X$ be the time until the next call in minutes. Since calls occur every $10$ minutes on average, the rate is  $\lambda =\frac{1}{10}$ calls per minute, and we can write

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{10}).
$$

Recall that exponential random variables have the memoryless property. Therefore, given two positive real numbers $s,t,$ we have that

$$
P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=P(X>t)={e}^{-\lambda t}.
$$

We can compute the complementary conditional probability as follows:

$$
P(X\le s+t\,|\,X>s)=1-P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=1-{e}^{-\lambda t}
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda =\frac{1}{10},$ $s=20,$ and $t=5.$ 

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 20+5\,|\,X>20) & =P(X\le 5) \\  & =1-{e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & =1-{e}^{-(1/10)\cdot (5)} \\  & =1-{e}^{-1/2} \\  & ≈0.393.\end{aligned}
$$
